source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed advertised specifications in a consumer product performance report

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Locate all records involving the failed specification.
3. For each record, remove any obvious outliers by the following method:

a.	Determine the upper and lower control limits for each test record as follows:

i.	If test record contains only one result then the upper and lower control limits is 3 * standard deviation around the central line.
ii.	If test record contains more than one result then first sum the number of results (both successful and failed) that were tested for the failed specifications and then divide that by 2.  This the central line or central tendency of the test results for the failed specification.  Then take the standard deviation of the successful results above the central tendency and the same again for failed results below the central tendency and add those together.  Finally multiply by 3 which is the upper and lower control limits.  

b.	If the upper limit is greater than the specification, then disregard any test
